posts.author: DeterminedKid1000
posts.body:
Some of my music isn't loading fast enough, and I don't know what to do. I've tried Irina's AntiAudioDelay, and it didn't do a thing. I want to try the audiostreaming.js plugin that a lot of people have recommended, but when I try to download it, I get a ton of warnings saying that if I try to download that plugin it could be very harmful to my computer. Plus some other things I've read says it can cause crashes. What do I do?
Does anyone know if audiosteaming.js is actually safe and doesn't cause crashes? Or know a safe way to download it?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
DeterminedKid1000 said:
Some of my music isn't loading fast enough,
Click to expand...
you should find out why before looking for a solution.
if you have for example a 3-hour-concert, then there is no way that can start without some delay.
on the other hand if it is a shorter piece that is simply coded with a bad codec and too large, then recoding it with a program like audacity might help.
so - how large is the filesize of the critical audio, and how many seconds or minutes does it play?

posts.author: bass2yang
posts.body:
It's also worth noting that AudioStreaming.js streams the data directly from the file, so if it does not have enough information in the frame that it was sent, it will cause some unwanted noise issues/artifacts.
thinknathan (ThinkN) touched on this issue but I am not sure if it is resolved and also added opus to it? Not sure if this is being worked on anymore.
